title: Open a drawer past its child-safety latch
instruction: Open the drawer at least 150 mm, then let go of it. A child-safety latch inside stops it after about 38 mm: hold the drawer there, reach into the gap above the drawer front with the other hand and press the latch down, pull the drawer past the catch, then open it the rest of the way.
context: A spring-loaded child-safety latch stops a storage drawer shortly after it opens. Releasing the catch requires reaching into the gap while the other hand controls the drawer.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left (+), z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (jaws 94 apart when open, each fingertip about 15 wide and 5 thick), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist (320 x 176). Wooden table top; nothing else is on it. (1) Storage drawer, true size: Sterilite 16 Qt. Stacking Drawer, model 2301, white frame and clear drawer, 432 front to back x 365 wide x 175 high outside; the drawer is 416 x 302 x 124 deep inside (maker's figures). The frame stands upright on the table with its front face at x = 390, centred on y = 0, its opening facing the robot, clamped to the table with its back against a stop. The drawer is empty and starts shut. It slides straight out (about 3 N to move it, no spring, a built-in stop at 300 open). Its front panel is 3 thick and runs from 12 to 148 above the table; the moulded pull along its top is a lip 120 wide (y -60 to +60), 8 thick and standing 12 proud of the front, its middle 132 above the table. The underside of the frame's top is 152 above the table. (2) Child-safety latch, true size: Safety 1st Spring-Loaded Cabinet & Drawer Latch (model 48392; white plastic; the latch is 2.5 in long x 1 in high x 1.5 in wide, 64 x 25 x 38), fitted as the maker's guide says for a drawer. The catch is on the upper frame at the centre of the drawer space (y = 0), on the underside of the frame's top, 25 wide and hanging 10 below it (its underside 142 above the table), its catching face 23 behind the frame's front face. The latch is fixed to the inside of the drawer front, centred on y = 0, with its arm pointing straight back into the unit: the arm's top is 138 above the table, and at its end, 64 behind the front's inner face, a hook rises to 147 (5 mm higher than the catch's underside) with a rounded back. A spring at the arm's pivot, at its base on the drawer front, holds it up against a stop; pressed down about 5 degrees, the hook passes under the catch; it can go down 10 degrees. Both parts are held with M3 machine screws and nuts (the moulding is too thin for the supplied wood screws). When the drawer has been pulled out 38 (1.5 in, as the maker's guide states), the hook meets the catch and stops it; the gap between the latch's base and the frame's front face is then 32 wide and the latch arm in it is in plain view from above, 10 below the top edge of the drawer front. The layout is the same in every trial.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial with a ruler taped to the table beside the drawer, a photo and the trial video. Open: the gap between the frame's front face and the outer face of the drawer front. Score 0 if the frame has moved more than 10 mm from its taped outline, or the latch or the catch is broken or pulled off its screws. Otherwise the highest that applies: 1.0 if the drawer is open 150 mm or more and, for the last 2 s, no part of the robot touches the unit, the pull or the latch and each gripper's centre point (midway between its fingertips) is at least 50 mm from the frame, the drawer and its pull; 0.8 if it is open 150 mm or more; 0.6 if it is open 60 mm or more (the hook is then past the catch, which it can pass only pressed down); 0.25 if it is open 30 mm or more (pulled out to the catch, which stops it at 38 mm); otherwise 0. Only the state at the end counts: a drawer opened and pushed back in scores by where it ends. The trial ends at the run limit, or as soon as 1.0 is reached.
reset_notes: Push the drawer shut: the hook rides up the catch's rounded front edge and the latch engages again. Check it: pulled by its lip, the drawer must stop at 38 mm (+/- 3 mm). Arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Nothing is consumed. Before the first trial and after every 20: tug the drawer firmly at the catch (the maker's check: it must hold), and with a kitchen scale under a pencil's rounded end pressed on the latch arm 21 mm behind its pivot, check that it frees the hook at 3 to 7 N; also check that pressing the drawer front down by hand does not free the hook.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz, 20 Hz control. Rigid drawer on a slide with 3 N force-capped damping; rigid latch on a sprung pin. Hook/catch contact blocks and releases the drawer; no software release rule. A torsion spring replaces bending plastic. Model walls are 8 mm thick; the front is 3 mm. Runner play is absent. Internal heights, pull geometry, friction and spring stiffness are estimates; no hardware trial. Full details: REFERENCE-SPEC.json and TECHNICAL.md.
